## Kriging for soil pH across ontario districts

```{r}
variogram = variogram(value_avg~1, soil_ontario) 
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Variogram of soil measurements(phH values) in Indiana. The number beside the points indicates the number of points from the variogram cloud that were in that particular bin."}
variogram |>
  plot(plot.numbers =TRUE,
       ylab =expression(gamma(h)),
       xlab = "Distance (h) in metres",
       pch =16)
```

```{r}
# different variogram models 
variogram_spherical  = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Sph", 50000, 1))
variogram_gaussian = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Gau", 40000, 1))
variogram_exponential = fit.variogram(variogram, vgm(1, "Exp", 50000, 1))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Visualizing different variogram models"}
#plot the various models
plot(gamma~dist, variogram,
     ylab =expression(gamma(h)),
     xlab = "Distance (h) in metres",
     pch =16)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_exponential, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'purple', lwd = 2)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_spherical, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'orange', lwd = 2)
lines(variogramLine(variogram_gaussian, 1.075 * max(variogram$dist)), 
      lty = 1, col = 'green', lwd = 2)
legend(x = "bottomright", legend = c("Exponential","Spherical","Gaussian"), 
       col = c("purple","orange","green"), 
       lty = c(1,1,1),
       lwd = c(2,2,2))
```

```{r, echo =FALSE, fig.cap = "Anisotropic sample variograms"}
# Anisotropic variogram models
variogram_anis = variogram(value_avg~1, soil_ontario, alpha = c(0,45,90,135))

variogram_anis |> ggplot(aes(x= dist, y=gamma))+
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(.~dir.hor)

```


```{r}
# block kriging to identify ideal pH
block_krige <- krige(value_avg~1, soil_ontario,
                     ontario_district, variogram_gaussian, block = c(10000, 10000))
```

```{r}
#block kriging for counties with ideal pH suitable for agriculture
block_krige$suitable <- ifelse(block_krige$var1.pred >= 6.0 &
                        block_krige$var1.pred <= 7.5,
                        "Suitable", "Not Suitable")

```



```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Comparing block-kriged averages (left-blues) to block-kriged averages (right-greens). Note that the green block-kriged values tend to define suitability better."}



# Plot 1: pH Range
gg1 <- ggplot(block_krige) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = var1.pred), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "pH Range") +  # or use scale_fill_distiller()
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  ggtitle("Block-Kriged pH Range")

# Plot 2: Suitability
gg2 <- ggplot(block_krige) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = suitable), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("lightgreen", "darkgreen"),
    name = "pH Suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +

  ggtitle("Districts with Suitable Soil pH")

# Arrange side-by-side
gg1 + gg2  # using patchwork


```

## Formating crop data for modeling

```{r}


# 1. Add lon/lat to original sf object
crop_hist_sf <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
  )

# 2. Pivot both yield and area to long format
yield_long <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("y"),
    names_to = "year",
    names_prefix = "y",
    values_to = "yield"
  )

area_long <- crop_hist_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("a"),
    names_to = "year",
    names_prefix = "a",
    values_to = "area"
  )

# 3. Join them back together
crop_long <- left_join(yield_long, area_long,
                       by = c("caruid", "crop", "year", "lon", "lat"))

# 4. Final touch: convert year to numeric
crop_long <- crop_long %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
dplyr::select(year, caruid, crop, yield, area, lon, lat) |>
dplyr:: filter(yield != -999, area != -999)|>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = crs)




```

build the INLA model

```{r}
formula <- yield ~ 
  f(ogf_id, model = "bym", graph = "ontario.graph") +
  f(year, model = "rw1") +
  f(crop, model = "iid") +
  area

result <- inla(
  formula, 
  family = "gaussian",  # or "gamma" if yield is skewed
  data = crop_ontario,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE)
)

```

## Soil Cleaning 

There are certain aspects of the soil that are important when it comes to crops.  For our analysis, we throught it would be best to focus on the texture, drainage, slope and the errosion factor of the soil.

```{r}
soil_clean <- dplyr::select(
  soil,
  ogf_id, atexture1, drainage1, slope1, k_factor1, cli1, cli_sys, acres, geometry
)

soil_clean %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%  # Remove geometry for summary
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)), .names = "na_{.col}"))


head(soil_clean)
```
#### Soil Kiging 

Soil properties do now change at a fast rate, so we are assuming they are constant over the time we collected crop and weather data.  Therefore, we employed kriging to the soil slope and erosion factor to find the average for each region.

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(cancensus)

#getting the ontario districts from Cancasus
# https://censusmapper.ca/api#api_overview
options(cancensus.api_key = "CensusMapper_b3e4e303dcb50fad4050328d7c3a8e67")
# Get Ontario's province code (35)
ontario_cd_sf <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",  # 2021 Census
  regions = list(PR = "35"),  # Ontario
  level = "CD",  # Census Division
  geo_format = "sf",  # Return as sf object
  labels = "short"
)
```
Getting the average slope for the areas

```{r}
krige_variable <- function(var_name, new_col_name, grid_sp) {
  # Ensure CRS consistency 
  corn_crs <- sf::st_crs(corn_data_sf)

  # Prep soil points (to corn CRS)
  soil_var <- soil_clean %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]])) %>%
    sf::st_transform(corn_crs) %>%
    sf::st_centroid(of_largest_polygon = TRUE)

  # gstat uses sp classes
  soil_sp <- as(soil_var, "Spatial")

  # Variogram 
  v <- gstat::variogram(as.formula(paste0(var_name, " ~ 1")), data = soil_sp)
  model <- gstat::fit.variogram(v, model = gstat::vgm(1, "Exp", 100000, 0.1))

  # Kriging 
  if (!isTRUE(sp::identicalCRS(grid_sp, as(soil_var, "Spatial")))) {
    sp::proj4string(grid_sp) <- sp::CRS(corn_crs$wkt)
  }

  kriged <- gstat::krige(
    as.formula(paste0(var_name, " ~ 1")),
    soil_sp,
    newdata = grid_sp,
    model = model,
    nmax = 30
  )

  kriged_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(kriged) %>%
    sf::st_set_crs(corn_crs)

  # One geometry per county
  counties <- corn_data_sf %>%
    dplyr::select(county, geom) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(county, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    sf::st_make_valid()

  # Spatial join once, then average by county 
  county_avg <- sf::st_join(kriged_sf, counties, join = sf::st_within) %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
    dplyr::group_by(county) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(!!new_col_name := mean(var1.pred, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  return(county_avg)  # county-level summary (no year)
}

```

```{r}
grid <- st_make_grid(corn_data_sf, cellsize = 5000, what = "centers") %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_set_crs(st_crs(corn_data_sf))

# Convert to Spatial for gstat
grid_sp <- as(grid, "Spatial")

```{r}
#kirging using function
slope_summary <- krige_variable("slope1", "slope1_avg", grid_sp)
kfactor_summary <- krige_variable("k_factor1", "kfactor_avg", grid_sp)

```

```{r}

  left_join(slope_summary, by = c("county")) %>%
  left_join(kfactor_summary, by = c("county")) %>%
  distinct(county, year, .keep_all = TRUE)
```


For the soil texture and drainage, we found the mode for each area.
```{r}
# 1) Recode fast (vector maps) --------------------------
tex_map <- c(
  CL="Clay Loam", SCL="Clay Loam", SICL="Clay Loam",
  SL="Sandy Loam", FSL="Sandy Loam", GSL="Sandy Loam", GL="Sandy Loam",
  GLS="Sandy Loam", VFSL="Sandy Loam", LVFS="Sandy Loam",
  L="Loam", SIL="Loam", VAR="Loam",
  C="Clay", SIC="Clay",
  S="Sand", FS="Sand", VFS="Sand", LS="Sand", LFS="Sand", CSL="Sand", LCS="Sand",
  ORG="Organic"
)

dr_map <- c(
  W="Well Drained", WA="Well Drained",
  MW="Moderately Well",
  P="Poorly Drained", VP="Poorly Drained",
  VR="Very Poor", VA="Very Poor", R="Very Poor",
  I="Imperfect"
)

soil_clean <- soil_clean %>%
  mutate(
    texture_group  = dplyr::recode(atexture1, !!!tex_map, .default = "Other"),
    drainage_group = dplyr::recode(drainage1, !!!dr_map, .default = NA_character_)
  )

# 2) Ensure same CRS once --------------------------------
corn_crs <- sf::st_crs(corn_data_sf)
if (!identical(sf::st_crs(soil_clean), corn_crs)) {
  soil_clean <- sf::st_transform(soil_clean, corn_crs)
}

# 3) One polygon per county (no year) --------------------
counties <- corn_data_sf %>%
  dplyr::select(county, geom) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(county, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid()

# (Optional) simplify county geometry if very complex
# counties <- sf::st_simplify(counties, dTolerance = units::set_units(50, "m"))

# 4) Spatial join soil -> county once --------------------
soil_by_county <- soil_clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(texture_group), !is.na(drainage_group)) %>%
  sf::st_join(counties, join = sf::st_within) %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry()

# 5) Modes via counts (fast) -----------------------------
texture_summary <- soil_by_county %>%
  dplyr::count(county, texture_group, name = "n") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(county) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(county, texture_mode = texture_group)

drainage_summary <- soil_by_county %>%
  dplyr::count(county, drainage_group, name = "n") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(county) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(county, drainage_mode = drainage_group)

# 6) Join back to county-year layer ----------------------
corn_data_sf <- corn_data_sf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(texture_summary,  by = "county") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(drainage_summary, by = "county")

```

  dplyr::left_join(slope_summary,    by = "county") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(kfactor_summary,  by = "county") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(texture_summary,  by = "county") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(drainage_summary, by = "county")

# Soybeans (rename to match key)
soybean_data_sf <- soybean_data_sf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(soil_feats, by = "county")
# (Optionally rename back after)

# Wheat

## Corn Yield

The corn growing season is from May-October. Before the forecasting, need to join the weather data for the growing season to the corn data. 
```{r}
#weather during the corn growing season for each year/station
weather_corn_gs <- weather %>%
  filter(month %in% 5:10)

if (anyNA(weather_corn_gs$total_precip)) {
  weather_na <- weather_corn_gs %>% dplyr::filter(is.na(total_precip))
  weather_ok <- weather_corn_gs %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(total_precip))
  if (nrow(weather_na) > 0 && nrow(weather_ok) > 0) {
    idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(weather_na, weather_ok)
    weather_corn_gs$total_precip[is.na(weather_corn_gs$total_precip)] <-
      weather_ok$total_precip[idx]
  }
}

head(weather_corn_gs)
colSums(is.na(weather_corn_gs))
```

# make sure corn_data_sf's active geometry is set (geom vs geometry)
if ("geom" %in% names(corn_data_sf)) {
  corn_data_sf <- sf::st_set_geometry(corn_data_sf, "geom")
}

# ensure same CRS
if (sf::st_crs(weather) != sf::st_crs(corn_data_sf)) {
  weather <- sf::st_transform(weather, sf::st_crs(corn_data_sf))
}

corn_regions <- corn_data_sf %>% dplyr::select(county, geom)
weather_with_county <- sf::st_join(weather_corn_gs, corn_regions, join = sf::st_nearest_feature)

# 5) Aggregate to county–year–month; ensure full May–Oct grid
weather_avg_complete <- weather_with_county %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(county, year, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_temp    = mean(mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_precip = mean(total_precip, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_humidity = mean(max_humidity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(county, year, month = 5:10)

# 6) Fill within county-month across years, then pivot to wide
weather_avg_filled <- weather_avg_complete %>%
  dplyr::group_by(county, month) %>%
  tidyr::fill(mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity, .direction = "downup") %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

weather_wide <- weather_avg_filled %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = month,
    values_from = c(mean_temp, total_precip, max_humidity),
    names_glue  = "{.value}_m{month}"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    county = stringr::str_squish(tolower(as.character(county))),
    year   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(year)))
  )

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#deature engineering
#it look a long time to run with the geometry- so dropping it to do the forecasting methods
# Robust year parser (handles "2024", "2024 ", "2024-01-01", etc.)
safe_scale <- function(x) {
  z <- as.numeric(scale(x))
  z[!is.finite(z)] <- NA_real_
  z
}

months <- 5:10
mt_cols <- paste0("mean_temp_m", months)
pr_cols <- paste0("total_precip_m", months)
hm_cols <- paste0("max_humidity_m", months)

corn_feats <- full_corn_data %>%
  mutate(
    gs_temp_avg     = rowMeans(across(all_of(mt_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    gs_precip_sum   = rowSums(across(all_of(pr_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    gs_humidity_avg = rowMeans(across(all_of(hm_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    slope1_z  = safe_scale(slope1_avg),
    kfactor_z = safe_scale(kfactor_avg),
    temp_z    = safe_scale(gs_temp_avg),
    precip_z  = safe_scale(gs_precip_sum),
    humid_z   = safe_scale(gs_humidity_avg)
  )

corn_feats <- corn_feats %>%
  mutate(
    texture_f  = fct_explicit_na(as.factor(texture_mode), na_level = "Unknown"),
    drainage_f = fct_explicit_na(as.factor(drainage_mode), na_level = "Unknown")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # optional but helpful if you have tiny categories; adjust min if needed
    texture_f  = fct_lump_min(texture_f,  min = 10),
    drainage_f = fct_lump_min(drainage_f, min = 10)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # choose sensible baselines (change if you prefer)
    texture_f  = fct_relevel(texture_f,  "Loam", after = 0),
    drainage_f = fct_relevel(drainage_f, "Well Drained", after = 0)
  )

#creating ids for INLA
county_levels <- corn_feats %>%
  distinct(county) %>%
  arrange(county) %>%
  pull(county)

corn_feats <- corn_feats %>%
  mutate(
    id      = as.integer(factor(county, levels = county_levels)),
    time_id = as.integer(factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year))))
  )
```
To set up to use INLA in the models, need to let it know that the counties are neighbours and can borrow information if needed.

#### 2024 Forecast for Corn

```{r}
# Train / test (unchanged except we now include the factors)
train_data <- corn_feats %>%
  filter(year <= 2023) %>%
  mutate(y = as.numeric(yield)) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, y,
         slope1_z, kfactor_z, temp_z, precip_z, humid_z,
         texture_f, drainage_f,
         id)

test_2024 <- corn_feats %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  mutate(y = NA_real_) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, y,
         slope1_z, kfactor_z, temp_z, precip_z, humid_z,
         texture_f, drainage_f,
         id)

stack_2024 <- bind_rows(train_data, test_2024) %>%
  mutate(time_id = as.integer(factor(year, levels = sort(unique(corn_feats$year))))) %>%
  dplyr::select(y, slope1_z, kfactor_z, temp_z, precip_z, humid_z,
         texture_f, drainage_f,
         id, time_id)



```

#### Autoregression 
```{r}
f_fixed <- y ~ 1 +
  slope1_z + kfactor_z + temp_z + precip_z + humid_z +
  texture_f + drainage_f

```

```{r}
fit_ar1 <- INLA::inla(
  update(f_fixed, . ~ . + f(time_id, model = "ar1") + f(id, model = "iid")),
  family = "gaussian",
  data = stack_2024,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute   = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE)
)

# Pull 2024 preds
n_train <- nrow(train_data)
pred_2024_ar1 <- fit_ar1$summary.fitted.values$mean[(n_train + 1):nrow(stack_2024)]

# 2024 predictions (the NA rows at the end)
pred_2024_ar1 <- fit_ar1$summary.fitted.values$mean[(n_train + 1):nrow(stack_2024)]

# Attach to test set (optional)
results_ar1 <- test_2024 %>%
  mutate(pred_yield_ar1 = pred_2024_ar1) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, pred_yield_ar1)
results_ar1

```
```{r}
# 1) Actuals for 2024
actual_2024 <- full_corn_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, actual_yield = yield)

#compute RMSE/MAE without external packages
#ar1 errors
calc_errors <- function(pred_df, model_name) {
  df <- pred_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(year == 2024) %>%
    dplyr::select(county, year, pred_yield_ar1) %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(actual_2024, by = c("county", "year")) %>%  # compare only matched rows
    dplyr::mutate(
      se = (actual_yield - pred_yield_ar1)^2,
      ae = abs(actual_yield - pred_yield_ar1)
    )

  by_county <- df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(county) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      RMSE = sqrt(mean(se, na.rm = TRUE)),
      MAE  = mean(ae, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Model = model_name)

  total <- df %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      county = "TOTAL",
      RMSE = sqrt(mean(se, na.rm = TRUE)),
      MAE  = mean(ae, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Model = model_name)

  dplyr::bind_rows(by_county, total)
}

# 3) Use it
errors_ar1 <- calc_errors(results_ar1, "AR1")

errors_ar1
```

#### Random Walk 1

```{r}
# Formula with RW1 on time_id
f_rw1 <- y ~ 1 + slope1_z + kfactor_z + temp_z + precip_z + humid_z +
  texture_f + drainage_f +
  f(time_id, model = "rw1") +   # random walk of order 1
  f(id, model = "iid")

# Fit model
fit_rw1 <- INLA::inla(
  f_rw1,
  family = "gaussian",
  data = stack_2024,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute   = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE)
)

# Extract 2024 predictions
pred_2024_rw1 <- fit_rw1$summary.fitted.values$mean[(n_train + 1):nrow(stack_2024)]

# Attach predictions to test set
results_rw1 <- test_2024 %>%
  mutate(pred_yield_rw1 = pred_2024_rw1)

# View predictions
results_rw1 %>% dplyr::select(county, year, pred_yield_rw1)
```

  left_join(weather_wide_soy, by = c("county", "year"))

full_soybean_data <- full_soybean_data %>%
  left_join(soil_info, by = c("county", "year"))

full_soybean_data<- full_soybean_data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    atexture1 = factor(atexture1),
    drainage1 = factor(drainage1)
  )

head(full_soybean_data)

```



#### Autoregression 
```{r}
#creating a lag to to capture the patterns from the previous time step
full_soybean_data <- full_soybean_data %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  mutate(yield_lag1 = dplyr::lag(yield, n = 1)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#training and test sets for the ar
soybean_train <- full_soybean_data %>% filter(year < 2024)
soybean_test <- full_soybean_data %>% filter(year == 2024)
```

```{r}
soybean_model_ar1_full <- lm(
  yield ~ yield_lag1 +
    mean_temp_m5 + mean_temp_m6 + mean_temp_m7 + mean_temp_m8 + mean_temp_m9 + 
    total_precip_m5 + total_precip_m6 + total_precip_m7 + total_precip_m8 + total_precip_m9 + 
    slope1 + k_factor1 + drainage1 + atexture1,
  data = soybean_train
)
```

```{r}
soybean_test$yield_pred_ar1 <- predict(soybean_model_ar1_full, newdata = soybean_test)
```

#### Random Walk 1

```{r}
# Random Walk 1: Predict 2024 yield as the 2023 yield (lag1)
full_soybean_data <- full_soybean_data %>%
  arrange(county, year) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  mutate(yield_rw1 = lag(yield, n = 1)) %>%  # 2023 yield for 2024 prediction
  ungroup()

soybean_rw1_2024 <- full_soybean_data %>%
  filter(year == 2024, !is.na(yield_rw1))

soybean_rw1_model <- lm(
  yield ~ yield_rw1 + mean_temp_m5 + mean_temp_m6 + mean_temp_m7 + mean_temp_m8 + mean_temp_m9 +
           total_precip_m5 + total_precip_m6 + total_precip_m7 + total_precip_m8 + total_precip_m9 +
           slope1 + k_factor1 + atexture1 + drainage1,
  data = soybean_rw1_2024
)

```

```{r}
#2024 forecast
soybean_rw1_2024 <- soybean_rw1_2024 %>%
  mutate(yield_pred_rw1_adjusted = predict(rw1_model, newdata = rw1_2024))
```

full_soybean_data <- full_soybean_data %>%

## 2025 Forecast

#### Corn

The autoregression performed the best, so using that.

Making a data set for 2025

```{r}
#train/test
#trainig on everything 2024 and before
train_data <- corn_feats %>%
  filter(year <= 2024) %>%
  mutate(y = as.numeric(yield)) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, y,
         slope1_z, kfactor_z, temp_z, precip_z, humid_z,
         texture_f, drainage_f, id)

#test set- 2025 data- creating blank column for 2025
test_2025 <- corn_feats %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  mutate(
    year = 2025,
    y = NA_real_
  )
n_train <- nrow(train_data)

stack_2025 <- bind_rows(train_data, test_2025) %>%
  mutate(time_id = as.integer(factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year)))))

#running rw1 from before
f_rw1 <- y ~ 1 +
  slope1_z + kfactor_z + temp_z + precip_z + humid_z +
  texture_f + drainage_f +
  f(time_id, model = "rw1") +
  f(id, model = "iid")

fit_rw1_2025 <- INLA::inla(
  f_rw1,
  family = "gaussian",
  data = stack_2025,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
  control.compute   = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE)
)

# Get predictions for the test rows
n_train <- nrow(train_data)
pred_2025_rw1 <- fit_rw1_2025$summary.fitted.values$mean[(n_train + 1):nrow(stack_2025)]

results_rw1_2025 <- test_2025 %>%
  mutate(pred_yield_rw1 = pred_2025_rw1) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, year, pred_yield_rw1)

results_rw1_2025
```
```{r}
yield_2024 <- corn_feats %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  dplyr::select(county, actual_yield = yield)

comparison_rw1 <- results_rw1_2025 %>%
  left_join(yield_2024, by = "county") %>%
  mutate(
    change = pred_yield_rw1 - actual_yield,
    direction = ifelse(change > 0, "Increase", "Decrease")
  )

map_data_rw1 <- corn_regions %>%
  mutate(county = tolower(county)) %>%
  left_join(
    comparison_rw1 %>% mutate(county = tolower(county)),
    by = "county"
  )

#plotting a map that shows wheather yield increases or decreasing per county
ggplot(map_data_rw1) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = direction), color = "gray30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increase" = "forestgreen", "Decrease" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    title = "Corn Yield Change in 2025 vs 2024",
    fill = "Direction of Change"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
